To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cloud is a good place to run applications that are designed to take advantage of it, and that the OS is not the only way to achieve this.
we have designed and implemented an operating system that is specifically tailored for cloud computing.

we introduce the concept of application-driven operating system (AppOS) compositions, where each application employs its own customized OS, that we show the feasibility of AppOS compositions by building and deploying two applications with different requirements on the OS, and that we show the benefits of AppOS compositions in terms of reduced resource usage and improved performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) understanding the implications of this new application model on the design of operating systems; (ii) developing a framework to enable application-driven OS composition; and (iii) exploring how to build efficient, secure and scalable operating systems in the cloud.
the following questions: How can we design an OS that is suitable for cloud computing?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OS is not dead in the cloud.
the cloud is a platform for innovation and that it is time to rethink the role of the operating system.
the cloud computing environment is a new paradigm that requires new ways to build and manage distributed applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new model for building cloud applications, which we call the Application-Driven Operating System (ADOS) Model.
we are proposing a model for distributed applications where the OS is no longer the central piece of the system, and instead, the application is.
we are proposing a way forward for operating system innovation in the cloud, by allowing applications to choose the OS they wish to use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can achieve a significant increase in the efficiency, scale, and functionality of applications by enabling OS innovation.
a new OS for the cloud can be built on top of existing OSes, without the need to rewrite the applications.
the OS is not the best place to implement the abstractions that are needed to build distributed applications for the cloud.
